scope: Input definition for the existing node-benchmark preparation route only
selection_basis: A fixed five-minute preparation horizon fits the already frozen five-minute review window and the six-minute/32-minute pilot windows. It is a bounded input definition chosen without model metrics, not a performance optimum.
neighborhood_rule: Keep nonconflicting native Event relations incident on the sampled node in the declared history, retaining the native subject/predicate roles. All retained endpoints are context; no recursive expansion.
event_time_policy: Use original integer UTC nanoseconds, not source publication order; perform no timestamp correction.
process_context_policy: Exclude a relation whose required native Subject ancestry is missing, conflicting, cyclic or starts after that relation's Event. A timing flag on an early witness does not label or automatically exclude the entire node lifetime.
metadata_predictor_policy: Exclude metadata fields without defensible availability at or before the anchor. Current offline definitions are review evidence, not accepted predictor fields.
partition_context_policy: All retained Events and sampled/context identities must remain within the assigned whole-group partition; merge or purge overlap before any export.
limitations: Existing window bounds accommodate this horizon but do not prove continuous telemetry coverage.
No current binary partitions exist; this definition does not supply labels or independent groups.
Any later horizon, neighborhood or feature change requires a new input-spec version and fresh context/split checks.
